title: 6 Best RingCentral Alternatives in 2026
summary: Six RingCentral alternatives compared for 2026, with published pricing. Why AI Receptionist answers questions but cannot change a booking.
body_markdown:
*Written by Punn Kam, ex-Google AI engineer and Y Combinator repeat founder. He is the co-founder of Conduit, an AI agent platform built for hospitality, serving 300+ hospitality brands in 140+ languages. Last updated August 28, 2026.*


Most people looking for a RingCentral alternative do not need a different phone system. They need something that finishes the call. RingCentral now ships AI Receptionist at $39 a month as an add-on, or $49 standalone, and it answers, routes, and handles FAQs. What it cannot do is change a booking, because it is trained on your website and uploaded documents rather than connected to your reservation system.


## Why do people leave RingCentral?


Three reasons come up repeatedly, and only one of them is about the phone system itself.


The first is seat pricing. RingEX is priced per user, which is the right unit for a sales floor and the wrong one for a property. If you run 200 units with four staff, you buy four seats and get a coverage model that has nothing to do with how many guests are calling.


Next, the AI answers rather than acts. RingCentral trains AI Receptionist on your website, FAQs, and uploaded documents. That is a knowledge base. It will tell a guest that checkout is 11am. It will not move that guest's checkout to 2pm, because it has no write access to a reservation it cannot see.


Last, stack sprawl. The phone lives in RingCentral, the guest thread lives somewhere else, and the reservation lives in the PMS. The guest explains the problem twice.


## What does RingCentral actually cost?


RingCentral publishes RingEX per user per month with up to 33% off for annual billing, and routes bundled add-ons to sales. AI Receptionist is published separately: $39 a month as an add-on to a RingEX plan, including 100 minutes, or $49 a month standalone, with more minutes sold in 100-minute bundles.


The number to model is not the seat price. It is the minutes. 100 minutes is under two hours of talk time a month, which a single property can burn through in a busy week.


## Which RingCentral alternatives are worth comparing?


Ordered by what unit they price on, because that is what decides whether the cost tracks your business.


Tool Priced on Autonomous voice agent Reads and changes a reservation


RingCentral Per user, AI Receptionist $39 add-on / $49 standalone Yes, AI Receptionist No, trained on documents


Dialpad Per user, conversation-based AI credits Yes, Dialpad AI Agent Not for hospitality systems


Quo (formerly OpenPhone) Per user, $19 / $33 / $47 monthly Yes, Sona No


Aircall Per license, 3 minimum Yes, AI Voice Agents No


Goodcall Per agent, $79 / $129 / $249 monthly Yes Zapier only, no PMS named


Smith.ai Per call, 30 calls for $300 AI-first or human-first CRM only, no PMS named


Conduit Per unit, from $18/unit/mo Yes, same agent as messaging Yes, write-back across connected PMSes


### Dialpad


The closest like-for-like swap. Dialpad AI Agent is described as autonomous across voice and digital, and pricing is conversation-based so credits are consumed when the AI does something. If you want a general business phone system with a capable agent, this is the straight substitution.


### Quo, formerly OpenPhone


Worth knowing that OpenPhone rebranded to Quo. Published at $19, $33, and $47 per user per month, dropping to $15, $23, and $35 on annual billing, with an AI agent called Sona that answers around the clock. The cheapest credible entry on this list, and the right answer for a small team that mostly needs a shared number handled well.


### Aircall


Essentials, Professional, and Custom, with a three-licence minimum on the first two and twenty-five on Custom. Its AI Voice Agents handle frequent questions autonomously and transfer to a human with context, which is a sensible design. The minimum seat count is the thing to check if your team is small.


### Smith.ai


A different model: you buy calls, not seats. 30 calls for $300, 90 for $810, 300 for $2,100, with overage from $8.50 to $11.50 a call and extras like $1.50 per appointment booked. You can pick AI-first or human-first. The economics only work at low call volume, and its named integrations are CRMs rather than property systems.


### Goodcall


$79, $129, and $249 per agent per month, or $66, $108, and $208 annually, with $0.50 per customer over the monthly limit. It targets salons, local service businesses, and BPO. Integration is via Zapier, with no property management system named.


### Conduit


Ours, so the criterion is stated rather than assumed: it is the option on this list built for the case where the caller has a reservation. Priced per unit from $18 a month rather than per seat, voice and text run on one agent so a guest who calls and then texts is not starting over, and it writes back to the PMS rather than only reading it. Our published automation band is 70-90% across the platform, and Cash Flow Street, a 35-property manager, runs at 96%. Watch-out: if your callers are not guests, none of that is worth paying for, and Dialpad or Quo is the better buy.


## Who should stay on RingCentral?


Most businesses, honestly. If you need desk phones, extensions, call queues, and a contact centre for a team of forty, RingCentral is a mature product doing a job that a hospitality agent does not do at all. AI Receptionist at $39 is competitive for straightforward answer-and-route work.


The switch only makes sense when the calls are about something the phone system cannot see. A guest asking to extend a stay, reset a door code, or move a checkout is asking for a change to a record that lives in your PMS. No amount of voice quality substitutes for access to it.

## FAQ


### How much does RingCentral AI Receptionist cost?


$39 a month as an add-on to a RingEX plan, including 100 minutes, or $49 a month standalone. Additional minutes are sold in 100-minute bundles.


### Can RingCentral AI Receptionist change a booking?


No. RingCentral trains it on your website, FAQs, and uploaded documents, so it answers from a knowledge base. Changing a reservation requires write access to the system holding it.


### What is the cheapest RingCentral alternative?


Quo, formerly OpenPhone, at $19 per user per month monthly or $15 annually. It includes an AI agent called Sona for call answering.


### Is RingCentral good for hotels?


It is a capable business phone system, and it is not hospitality software. It has no property management system integration, so it can answer questions about your property but cannot act on a guest's reservation.


### What should I ask an AI phone vendor before switching?


Two questions settle most of it. What can the agent change, not just read. And what unit am I priced on, seats or units, because that decides whether the bill tracks the business.
